1051:
(a) An occupation tax is hereby levied upon those businesses and practitioners of professions and occupations with one or more locations or offices in the corporate limits of the city, and/or upon the applicable out-of-state businesses with no location or office in Georgia pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-7, and upon real estate brokers, agents, or companies that sell real property located in the city. The occupation tax amount shall be determined by the sum of two (2) components:
(1) A nonrefundable annual administrative fee, and
(2) An appropriate tax amount determined by tax rates based upon gross receipts of the business or practitioner in combination with the profitability ratio for the type of business, profession, or occupation, as measured by nationwide averages derived from statistics, classifications, or other information published by the U.S. Office of Management and Budget, the U.S. Census Bureau, the U.S. Internal Revenue Service, or successor agencies of the United States.
(b) For the purpose of determining occupation tax, it shall be assumed that every business or practitioner has at least one (1) employee.
(c) The mayor and council shall by resolution, from time to time, establish the administrative fee, the per employee tax and a tax schedule to set the occupation tax determined by profitability ratios in combination with gross receipts for each business, trade, profession, or occupation.
(d) The occupation tax clerk shall classify the entire gross receipts of the applicant by the dominant line or product of the applicant.
(e) Where the gross receipts of a business or practitioner do not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000.00) in a year, or where federal or state law precludes the imposition of a gross receipts taxes on a particular class of business, trade, occupation or profession, including but not limited to the airline industry, which business, trade or occupation is otherwise subject to taxation by the city, such occupation tax levied shall be based only upon the number of employees of the business or practitioner and the administrative fee.
(f) Real estate brokers, agents, or companies that sell real property located in the city but that do not maintain a principal or branch office within the city shall only have taxes levied upon them based on the administrative fee and profitability ratios in combination with gross receipts.
(g) (1) No business or practitioner shall be required to pay more than one (1) occupation tax for each of its locations.
(2) No occupation tax will be required upon more than one hundred (100) per cent of a business's gross receipts.
(3) No occupation tax will be required on receipts on which such tax has been lawfully levied and paid in other localities or states.
(4) An occupation tax shall be required from real estate brokers, agents, or companies whose offices are located outside the taxing jurisdiction, and who sell property inside the city.
(5) An occupation tax shall not be levied in any manner other than that described in this section.
(6) Occupation taxes are limited to the gross receipts earned in the taxing jurisdiction or in the state.
(7) Out-of-state businesses with no location in Georgia shall be assessed occupation taxes based on the gross receipts of the business, as provided in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-7, which are reasonably attributable to sales or services in the state.
(Ord. No. 2013-13, § 1, 11-4-13)

(2) Any change of business ownership; or
(3) The termination of any business or occupation.
(Ord. No. 2013-13, § 1, 11-4-13)
1072:

(Ord. No. 2013-13, § 1, 11-4-13)
1073:
(a) Each and every business that ceases operations in the city or has otherwise been required to register and pay the occupation tax must file a final return with the occupation tax clerk and pay an administrative fee for the processing of the final return.
(b) If a business ceases operation within a year for which an occupation tax has been paid or credited, the tax shall be refundable, upon request, if, after a final return is filed and after the actual tax liability is calculated, the business tax credited exceeds that liability. Every amusement game room in the city shall comply with the proximity provision for businesses licensed to sell alcohol as set out in O.C.G.A. § 3-3-21 and chapter 3 of this Code. No amusement game room in the city shall offer to the public more than nine (9) bona fide coin operated amusement machines offering non-cash redemption in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 16-12-35(c) and (d)(1)(2), or both at the same location. (Ord. No. 2012-05, § 3, 2-20-12)

(Ord. No. 2012-05, § 3, 2-20-12)
1087:
(a) In addition to penalties set out in the O.C.G.A. provisions for failure to comply with the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 16-12-35(a) through (i), the owner or operator of an amusement game room, after conviction in a court of competent jurisdiction, and a hearing before the mayor and council, may be subject to the following penalties:
(1) First offense: Suspension for not more than six (6) months of the owner or proprietor's license for offering any amusement game at the location where the violation occurred.
(2) Second offense: Suspension for not more than twelve (12) months of the owner or proprietor's license for offering any amusement game at the location where the violation occurred.
(3) Third offense: Suspension or permanent revocation of the owner or proprietor/operator's license for offering any amusement game at the location where the violation occurred, and suspension of other permits and licenses granted by the city for not more than six (6) months.
(b) Penalties for violation of the provisions of this article by the owner or operator of an amusement game room, after conviction in the municipal court of the city are as follows:
(1) First offense: Fine not to exceed five hundred dollars ($500.00) for each violation.
(2) Second offense: Fine not to exceed seven hundred fifty dollars ($750.00) for each violation, suspension of the owner or operator's license for offering any amusement game at the location for not more than three (3) months, or both.
(3) Third offense: Fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) for each violation, suspension or permanent revocation of the owner or operator's license for offering any amusement game at the location, or suspension of other permits and licenses granted by the city for not more than six (6) months, or any combination of these penalties.
(c) The fines listed in the penalties for violation of this article may be imposed by the judge of the municipal court of the city. Suspension or revocation of the owner or operator's license for offering any amusement game at the location where the violation occurred, and suspension of other permits and licenses granted by the city may be imposed by the mayor and council after a hearing.
(d) Offering one or more bona fide coin operated amusement machine games in violation of an order suspending or revoking the license for the offering of any amusement game at the location is punishable, after conviction in the municipal court of the city, by a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), imprisonment not to exceed thirty (30) days, or both such fine and imprisonment.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, § 3, 2-20-12)
1088:
The municipal court of the city is authorized to impose the following penalties on any person convicted of receiving money as a reward for the successful play or winning of any bona fide coin operated amusement machine from any person owning, possessing, controlling or overseeing such bona fide coin operated amusement machine or any person employed by or acting on behalf of a person owning, possessing, controlling or overseeing a bona fide coin operated amusement machine.
(1) First offense: Fine not to exceed two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) for each violation.
(2) Second and subsequent offense: Fine not to exceed five hundred dollars ($500.00) for each violation.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, § 3, 2-20-12)
1089:
All businesses operating as an amusement center hereunder shall be subject to the following regulations:
(1) Devices to be kept in plain view; gambling devices prohibited. All machines shall at all times be kept and placed in plain view of and open and accessible to any person(s) who may frequent or be in any place of business where such machines are kept or used. Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize, permit or license any gambling device of any nature whatsoever.
(2) Inspection. The chief of police shall inspect or cause the inspection of any place or building in which any such machine(s) are operated or set up for operating, and shall inspect, investigate and test such machines as needed.
(3) Attendant required. It shall be unlawful for any proprietor to open his business to the public unless an attendant is present. Said attendant shall be of sufficient mental and physical capacity so as to be able to provide aid to patrons if needed or desired. Said attendant shall not be less than eighteen (18) years of age.
(4) Loitering. As used in this section, "loitering" shall mean remaining idle in essentially one location and shall include the concepts of spending time idly, loafing or walking about aimlessly, and shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation licenses to operate an amusement center to permit loitering on or in the immediate vicinity of any machine or business premises regulated hereunder in such a manner as to:
a. Create or cause to be created a danger of a breach of the peace;
b. Create or cause to be created any disturbance or annoyance to the comfort and repose of any person;
c. Obstruct the free passage of pedestrians or vehicles;
d. Obstruct, molest or interfere with any person lawfully in a public place.
e. Shirt and shoes required. All proprietors shall require shirts and shoes to be worn at all times by any person frequenting their premises.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, § 3, 2-20-12)
1090:
In the event that it comes to the attention of the mayor and council that an amusement center has created a nuisance to the surrounding community or the operator or proprietor has violated any provision of this section, the following procedure will be followed:
(1) The city clerk shall issue a notice of objection which shall include the address of the location and the specific reasons why the amusement center in question is alleged to be a nuisance or alleged to be in violation of any provision of this section. The city clerk will then notify the proprietor that a notice of objection has been filed and will set a date for a hearing before the mayor and council. Extensions and necessary investigations will be granted and conducted at the discretion of the city clerk.
(2) At the time of the hearing, any resident, the operator, the proprietor and the city clerk or other witnesses may be heard. Thereafter, the mayor and council shall issue a notice of decision which will call for the dismissal of the objection, removal of the machines or such other remedy as they deem appropriate under the circumstances that are consistent with the purpose of this section.
(3) The decision of the mayor and council shall be in writing and shall state the reasons for their decision and shall be based upon the merits of the case.
(4) The decision of the mayor and council shall be binding upon the proprietor and operator of the amusement center under consideration, subject to appeal to the proper court.
(Ord. No. 2012-05, § 3, 2-20-12)

(Ord. No. 2012-05, § 3, 2-20-12)
1096:
The following definitions shall apply in the interpretation and enforcement of this article:
Massage. The term "massage" (or "massages") as used in this article, shall be construed and deemed to mean any manner of manipulation, including, but not limited to, the rubbing, touching, stroking, kneading or vibrating of the superficial parts of the body, by direct or indirect physical contact with any portion of the body of a "massage technician, " as herein defined, or by any form of contact with a "massage apparatus, " as herein defined.
Massage apparatus. The term "massage apparatus," as used in this article, shall be construed and deemed to mean any manual, mechanical, hydraulic, hydrokinetic, electric or electronic device or instrument, or any device or instrument operated by manual, mechanical, hydraulic, hydrokinetic or electric power, which is utilized by a "massage technician," as herein defined, for the purpose of administering a massage, as herein defined.
Massage establishment. The term "massage establishment," as used in this article, shall be construed and deemed to mean any business established for profit which employs one (1) or more "massage technicians," as herein defined, or owns and operates or maintains for profit one (1) or more "massage apparatus," as herein defined to include, but not be limited to, bath house equipment, and which, for a good or valuable consideration, offers to the public facilities and personnel for the administration of "massages," as herein defined.
Massage technician. The term "massage technician," as used in this article, shall be construed and deemed to mean any person, whether male or female, whether or not a masseur or masseuse by profession, who, by direct or indirect physical contact with the body of another, or by use and operation of a "massage apparatus," as herein defined, and for any good or valuable consideration, administers a massage, as herein defined.
(Ord. No. 96-12, § 1, 4-1-96)
1097:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the practice as a massage technician, or any person, partnership, firm, corporation or other entity to operate a massage establishment without first having obtained the license required by this article.
(b) The license fee for a massage technician shall be fifty dollars ($50.00) per year.
(c) The license fee for a massage establishment shall be fifty dollars ($50.00) per year.
(Ord. No. 96-12, § 1, 4-1-96)
1101:
In administering massages under this article, the conditions of the massage room shall meet the standards set forth in section 11-54, and no activity shall occur between the massage technician and the patron which would be in violation of the criminal laws of the State of Georgia.
(Ord. No. 96-12, § 1, 4-1-96)
1103:
(a) The city clerk shall refuse to grant a license to an applicant or suspend or revoke a licensee under this article upon a finding that the licensee or applicant has:
(1) Displayed an inability or has become unable to work as a massage technician or as an operator of a massage establishment, as the case may be, with reasonable skill and safety to clientele by reason of illness, use of alcohol, drugs, narcotics, chemicals, or any other type of substance, or as a result of any mental or physical condition. In enforcing this paragraph, the city clerk may, upon reasonable grounds, require the licensee or applicant to submit to a mental or physical examination by an appropriate licensed practitioner of the healing arts. The expense of such examination shall be borne by such licensee or applicant. The results of such examination shall be admissible in any hearing before the city or a court of competent jurisdiction in the event of an appeal. If a licensee or applicant fails to submit to such an examination when properly directed to do so by the city, unless such failure was due to circumstances beyond the licensee's or applicant's control, the city may enter a final order upon proper notice, hearing, and proof of such refusal; or
(2) Been convicted in the last five (5) years of the following offenses: sodomy, aggravated sodomy, or solicitation of sodomy; masturbation for hire; public indecency; prostitution; solicitation of prostitution; pimping; pandering or pandering by compulsion; distribution of materials that are of obscene [nature] or depicting nudity or sexual conduct as defined under state law; any offense involving the use or threat of force or violence upon the person(s) of another; any offense involving narcotics, dangerous drugs or dangerous weapons; or any felony involving moral turpitude. For purposes of this section, a conviction shall include a finding or verdict of guilty, plea of guilty, or a plea of nolo contendere in a criminal proceeding; or
(3) Knowingly made a misleading, deceptive, untrue or fraudulent representation to a client, customer, or other person or entity in connection with the provisions of massage services or any document connected therewith; or committed an act of fraud or deceit or made any false statement in obtaining or attempting to obtain a license provided for in this article; or
(4) Performed massage services contrary to this article; or knowingly aided, assisted, procured, or advised any person to perform massage services contrary to this article; or knowingly performed any act which in any way aids, assists, procures, advises, or encourages any unlicensed person to perform massage services; or
(5) Engaged in any unprofessional, unethical, deceptive, or deleterious practice harmful to the public, which conduct or practice need not have resulted in actual injury to any person. For purposes of this section, unprofessional conduct shall also include any departure from or failure to conform to the acceptable minimum standards applicable to massage technicians or operators of massage establishments; or
(6) Failed to report to the city any act or omission of a licensee or applicant or any other person who violates the provisions of this article.
(b) In the event the city clerk denies an application for a license or finds that a license should be revoked or suspended pursuant to subsection (a) of this section, notice of such denial, suspension, or revocation shall be transmitted to the applicant or licensee, in writing, with the reasons for that action specified. The applicant or licensee shall have the right to appeal such denial, suspension, or revocation to the city manager. Such appeal shall be filed in writing no later than ten (10) days from the date of the city clerk's decision. A hearing shall be held within thirty (30) days from the date of the written notice of appeal. Within thirty (30) days from the date of the conclusion of the hearing, the city manager shall notify the applicant or licensee, in writing, of his recommendation and the reason therefor.
(c) For purposes of this section, a licensee or applicant, whether the same is a person, partnership, firm, corporation or other entity, who may or may not perform massage services, and all persons having a beneficial interest in the operation of a massage establishment (except stockholders owning less that five (5) per cent of the stock in a corporation) shall be subject to the provisions of this section and be treated as if they were the licensee or applicant.
(d) Where the city refuses to grant a license to an applicant or has revoked a license under this article, the affected licensee or applicant shall be disqualified from reapplying for such license for twelve (12) months immediately following such action taken by the city.
(Ord. No. 96-12, § 1, 4-1-96)

1107:

Installation of all equipment in such establishments shall be in conformity with the codes and ordinances relating to such installations.

1109:
(a) Premises used for self-service laundries must be kept in a clean and sanitary condition.
(b) No refuse of any kind shall be permitted to accumulate on such premises; and the premises shall be kept free from rats, mice and vermin.
(c) It shall be unlawful to employ any person afflicted with a venereal or any contagious disease in a self-service laundry.

1110:
It shall be unlawful to keep any such establishment open for business between 12:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. unless there is an adult attendant in charge of the premises during such hours.
(Code 1963, § 14-43)
1113:
(a) A "yard sale" is defined as the sale or trading of clothing, furniture, household items, food, dishes, antiques or similar goods or merchandise on a residentially zoned lot or parcel. The definition of yard sale shall include sales or trading of goods as outlined above, when fifty (50) per cent or more of the frontage on the street upon which the lot or parcel to be used fronts, is still used for residential purposes, even if such lot or parcel to be used is not residentially zoned. The term "yard sale" shall include garage sales, carport sales and similar types of sales or events.
(b) The individual in charge of the premises upon which the sale is conducted shall control the parking of vehicles of patrons so as to avoid congestion and hazardous conditions. Failure to do so shall be sufficient cause for the sale to be immediately terminated.
(c) Yard sales shall be allowed on a lot or parcel for not more than two (2) sales not to exceed two (2) days each during a twelve (12) month period. No individual shall be associated with or involved in yard sales for more than two (2) sales during a twelve-month period. No individual shall engage in the business of promoting or conducting yard sales for other persons for a fee or other consideration. Yard sales are prohibited on Sundays.
(d) Notice shall be provided to the police department of the city twenty-four (24) hours in advance of holding a yard sale. Such notice may be given by telephone, in writing, or by personal appearance at the police station.
(e) Advertising of merchandise for sale or trading or display of goods and merchandise as defined above for public viewing, shall be deemed a yard sale when conducted in a residentially zoned area or on a block where fifty (50) per cent or more of the frontage on the street upon which the lot or parcel to be used fronts, is still used for residential purposes, even if such lot or parcel to be used is not residentially zoned. Such goods or merchandise do not need to be attended for a sale to be deemed to be in existence.
(f) Violation of this section shall be deemed an offense and each day of violation shall be considered a separate offense.
(Ord. No. 97-01, § 1, 2-3-97)
1116:
For the purposes of this article, the following terms shall have the respective meanings ascribed to them:
Fire and other altered goods sale: A sale held out in such manner as to reasonably cause the public to believe that the sale will offer goods damaged or altered by fire, smoke, water or other means.
Going-out-of-business sale: A sale held out in such a manner as to reasonably cause the public to believe that upon the disposal of the stock or goods on hand the business will cease and be discontinued, including but not limited to the following sales: adjuster's, adjustment alteration, assignees', bankrupt, benefit of administrator, benefit of creditors, benefit of trustees, building coming down, closing, creditors committee, creditors, end, executor, final days, forced out, forced out of business, insolvent's last days, lease expires, liquidation, loss of lease, mortgage sale, receiver's, trustee's, and quitting business.
Goods: Any goods, wares, merchandise or other property capable of being the object of a sale regulated hereunder.
Removal of business sale: A sale held out in such a manner as to reasonably cause the public to believe that the person conducting the sale will cease and discontinue business at the place of sale upon disposal of the stock of goods on hand and will then move to and resume business at a new location in the city or will then continue business from another existing location in the city.
(Code 1963, § 14-73)
1117:
The provisions of this article are intended to augment and be in addition to the provisions of the general licensing regulations of the city and the regulations of this Code. When this article imposes a greater restriction upon persons, premises, businesses or practices than is imposed by the general licensing regulations of the city or other regulations of this Code, this article shall control.
(Code 1963, § 14-72)
1118:
A license issued by the city clerk shall be obtained by any person before selling or offering to sell any goods at a sale to be advertised or held out by any means to be one (1) of the following kinds:
(1) Going-out-of-business sale;
(2) Removal-of-business sale; and
(3) Fire and other altered-stock sale.
(Code 1963, § 14-74)
1119:
A person desiring to conduct a sale regulated by this article shall make a written application to the city clerk setting forth and containing the following information:
(1) Owner of goods: The true name and address of the owner of the goods to be the object of the sale.
(2) Previous owner of goods: The true name and address of the person from whom applicant purchased the goods to be sold and the price thereof, and if not purchased, the manner of such acquisition.
(3) Description of premises: A description of the place where such sale is to be held.
(4) Nature, term of occupant: The nature of the occupancy, whether by lease or sublease and the effective date of the termination of such occupancy.
(5) Period of sale: The dates of the period of time in which the sale is to be conducted.
(6) Reason for sale: A full and complete statement of the facts in regard to the sale, including the reason for the urgent and expeditious disposal of goods thereby and the manner in which the same will be conducted.
(7) Advertising: The means to be employed in advertising such sale together with the proposed content of any advertisement.
(8) Inventory: A complete and detailed inventory of the goods to be sold at such sale as disclosed by the applicant's records. Said inventory shall be attached to and become part of the required application.
(Code 1963, § 14-75)
1120:
(a) Bona fide orders: All goods included in the inventory required in section 11-103 shall have been purchased by the applicant for resale on bona fide orders without cancellation privileges and shall not comprise goods purchased on consignment.
(b) Goods purchased for sale hereunder: Such inventory shall not include goods ordered in contemplation of conducting a sale regulated hereunder. Any unusual purchase, or additions to the stock of goods of the business hereby affected within thirty (30) days before the filing of an application hereunder shall be deemed to be of such character.
(Code 1963, § 14-76)
1121:
A license shall be issued or renewed hereunder on the following terms:
(1) Licensing period: The license shall authorize the sale described in the application for a period of not more than thirty (30) consecutive days, Sundays and legal holidays excluded, following the issuance thereof.
(2) Renewal procedure: The city clerk shall renew a license for one (1) period of time only, such period to be in addition to the thirty (30) days permitted in the original license and not to exceed thirty (30) consecutive days, Sundays and holidays excluded, when he finds:
(a) That facts exist justifying the license renewal.
(b) That the licensee has filed an application for renewal.
(c) That the licensee has submitted with the application for renewal a revised inventory showing the items listed on the inventory remaining unsold and not listing any goods not included in the original application and inventory. 1133:
As used in this article, the following terms shall have the respective meanings ascribed to them:
(1) Transient merchant: Any person who sets up or displays merchandise for sale outside of a building on any lot where the person or entity setting up or displaying such merchandise does not also lawfully conduct business regularly in a building located on that lot.
(2) Peddler: Any person who solicits, excluding, however:
a. Transient merchants;
b. Any person who sells agricultural, forestry or other farm products;
c. Any person who conducts business at any industry or association trade show;
d. Any person who sells items at a rummage, garage, antique or similar sale, or a flea market, where such sale is not part of the regular business activity of such person; and
e. Any person who exclusively donates the net proceeds of all sales or moneys otherwise obtained to one (1) or more nonprofit organizations.
(3) Solicit shall mean taking orders, selling, or seeking orders or clients for the purchase of goods, wares, merchandise, foodstuffs, products, subscriptions, or services of any kind, character, or description whatsoever.
(4) Nonprofit organization: Any tax-exempt organization within the meaning of the Internal Revenue Code or the Georgia Income Tax Law, as such code and such law are now or may be hereafter amended.
(5) Nonprofit activities: Solicitation of funds or donations as a peddler or transient merchant for any nonprofit organization.
(6) Seasonal items: Christmas trees sold in October, November and December, and pumpkins sold in October.
(7) Special Events: Any event sponsored by the city, and any parade permitted by the city.
(8) Mobile food vehicle shall mean a motorized wheeled vehicle or a towed wheeled vehicle designed and equipped to serve food.
(9) Mobile food vendor shall mean the operator of a mobile food vehicle.
(10) Food retailer shall mean a food establishment that sells to consumer customers food or food products intended for preparation or consumption off of the premises.

1141:
(a) Any person desiring to conduct nonprofit activities in the city shall register with and obtain a written permit to conduct nonprofit activities from the city clerk. Permits for nonprofit activities shall be issued without charge.
(b) Any person desiring a permit to conduct nonprofit activities in the city shall file, on a form to be supplied by the city clerk, an application containing the following:
(1) Name of the applicant;
(2) Permanent home address of the applicant;
(3) Name and address of nonprofit organization or organizations to be represented;
(4) Names and addresses of any persons conducting or assisting in the conduct of nonprofit activities on behalf of applicant;
(5) Nature of any merchandise, wares, goods or any similar items to be sold or offered for sale or given away in conjunction with the nonprofit activities;
(6) Proof of tax-exempt status;
(7) Location or locations where nonprofit activities will be conducted.
(8) Sufficient documentation indicating that 11-48(d)(5) of this section has been satisfied.
(9) An agreement to fully indemnify and hold harmless the City of College Park and it officials, employees and agents from any and all causes of actions related to the conduct of nonprofit activities.
(c) Upon proper registration with the city clerk, a written permit shall be issued to be valid for a period of sixty (60) days from the date of issuance. In addition, identity cards shall be issued which must be carried by all persons while engaged in nonprofit activities.
(d) Nonprofit activities shall be subject to the following regulations:
(1) They shall only occur between 9:00 a m. and 5:00 p.m. (or 9:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. during daylight savings time) from Thursday through Sunday.
(2) The number of representatives conducting nonprofit activities for any single nonprofit organization shall not exceed ten (10) in number at any one time.
(3) Immediately prior to soliciting any person within the city, each representative shall present his or her identity card, issued by the city clerk, to each person solicited. Further, each representative must inform each person solicited as to any minimum donation required for the acceptance of any merchandise, wares, goods, or any similar items given by each representative prior to such acceptance by each person solicited.
(4) The representatives conducting nonprofit activities must each be at least eighteen (18) years of age.
(5) Each organization, group or person conducting nonprofit activities must secure sufficient insurance to cover risk of damage to persons or property while conducting nonprofit activities. The City of College Park must be named as an additional insured for any nonprofit activities conducted within fifteen (15) feet of a right-of-way. In the alternative, each organization, group or person conducting nonprofit activities must secure a letter of credit or surety bond in the amount of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) to ensure compliance with this section, with the City of College Park named as the obligee.
(e) It shall be unlawful for a representative of a nonprofit organization to:
(1) Falsely represent, directly or by implication, that funds are being solicited on behalf of any nonprofit organization other than the one registered with the city clerk.
(2) Without the express prior permission of any occupant or property owner, solicit at any residence, apartment complex, or shopping mall, other than areas open to public parking, where there is posted any sign forbidding any solicitation.
(3) Remain on private premises after being asked to leave the premises or continue solicitation after being refused upon the public streets, areas or parks; such action shall constitute harassment.
(4) Solicit at any residence where there is posted in plain view a sign reading as follows: "No Solicitors" or "No Peddlers."
(5) With respect to any person conducting nonprofit activities on or within fifteen (15) feet of any public right-of-way, to conduct its business in such a manner that the flow of vehicular traffic is impeded. Specifically, conduct of nonprofit activities from travel lanes shall not be permitted; provided however, that walking alongside a line of cars may only be permitted if the person conducting nonprofit activities stays out of the travel lanes and the conduct of nonprofit activities occurs when the traffic light is red and cars are stopped. Additionally, no sales or gifts to vehicle occupants shall be permitted.
(f) Any person violating any of the provisions of this section shall, upon conviction thereof, be subject to punishment as provided in section 1-8 for each offense.
(Ord. No. 2001-20, § 9, 9-4-01; Ord. No. 2007-21, § 1, 6-4-07)

1145:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, or offer for sale, food of any type from a mobile food vehicle without a license first having been granted under this section, except for such activities conducted in connection with city-sponsored events.
(b) An application for a permit hereunder shall be submitted to the city clerk or his or her designee setting forth all information required hereunder and in compliance with this section. The city clerk or his or her designee shall develop a form of application for the purpose of compliance with this article. The application shall be accompanied by an executed indemnity agreement indemnifying and releasing the city, its agents, employees and elected officials from any and all liability against any and all claims, actions and suits of any type whatsoever arising in connection with the activities of the mobile food vendor pursuant to the permit issued hereunder.
(c) The following information shall be provided with each application for a mobile food vehicle permit, along with an executed release and indemnification agreement provided by the city:
(1) Name of the mobile food vendor;
(2) Make, model and license plate number of the mobile food vehicle;
(3) Owner's contact information;
(4) Operator's contact information;
(5) Copy of approved permit from the Fulton County Health Department, or, if the mobile food vehicle will be operating in the portion of the city located in Clayton County, the Clayton County Health Department;
(6) List of operating locations and times including map detailing the position of the vehicle, and current zoning in said locations;
(7) Signatures from property owners indicating consent for the use of their property; and
(8) Signature of applicant indicating agreement to the listed requirements.
(d) Mobile food vendors shall be licensed and taxed in accordance with the provisions of section 11-145 of the City of College Park Code of Ordinances.
(e) No mobile food vendor shall conduct business or operate in the public right-of-way or on public property (including, but not limited to, public parks or public recreation grounds of the city (as defined in section 13-6(d) of the College Park Code of Ordinances)), without a special event permit. Mobile food vehicles cannot be parked in the public right-of-way, on sidewalks, grass, or areas not intended for parking vehicles.
(f) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in section 13-6(b) of the College Park Code of Ordinances, persons who are not an employee, officer or agent of the city or a resident of the city may enter public parks or public recreation grounds of the city to make purchases from mobile food vehicles lawfully conducting business or operating in public parks or public recreation grounds of the city pursuant to a special event permit.
(g) A mobile food vehicle may operate on private property subject to the following:
(1) The owner must provide prior written consent; and
(2) The mobile food vehicle must operate in accordance with the distance requirements set forth in section 11-152(m).
A mobile food vehicle shall not be allowed to park overnight on any private property without the prior written consent of the owner.
(h) Notwithstanding anything in this article to the contrary, a mobile food vendor shall maintain a one million dollar ($1,000,000.00) liability insurance policy. Proof of current liability insurance, issued by an insurance company licensed to do business in Georgia, protecting the Mobile Food Vendor, the public and the city from all claims for damage to property and bodily injury, including death, which may arise from operation under or in connection with the permit, shall be provided to the city as part of its permit application. If the mobile food vendor does not have insurance, the mobile food vendor may be under the umbrella of an existing business with the business' permission to do so. Such arrangement documentation shall be included with the application to the city.
(i) A mobile food vehicle shall not make sounds or announcements to call attention to the mobile food vehicle either while traveling on the public rights-of-way or when stationary. At all times said mobile food vehicle shall be in compliance with the city's noise ordinance.
(j) The license under which a mobile food vehicle is operating must be firmly attached and visible on the mobile food vehicle at all times.
(k) Any driver of a mobile food vehicle must possess a valid Georgia driver's license.
(l) Mobile food vehicles shall not be located within fifteen (15) feet of any street intersection or pedestrian crosswalk or ten (10) feet of any driveway.
(m) Mobile food vehicles shall not be located within two hundred (200) feet of a restaurant or a food retailer. Notwithstanding the foregoing:
(1) If a restaurant (or the corporate entity that owns the restaurant) owns a mobile food vehicle, the mobile food vehicle may be located within two hundred (200) feet of that restaurant; or
(2) If a mobile food vehicle is operating pursuant to a special event permit, the mobile food vehicle may be located within two hundred (200) feet of a restaurant or a food retailer.
(n) A mobile food vendor shall not sell or offer to sell any goods, foods, products, or services between the hours of 10:00 p.m. to 9:00 a.m.
(o) Vending structures shall not be left unattended or stored at any time on the open vending site when vending is not taking place or during restricted hours of operation.
(p) Mobile food vendors shall comply with all state, federal and local health and safety regulations and requirements and shall obtain and maintain any and all licenses required by any other health organization or governmental organization having jurisdiction over this subject matter.
(q) The following safety regulations shall apply to any and all vehicles operating under this article or used for mobile retail food establishments:
(1) Every vehicle shall be equipped with a reverse gear signal alarm with a sound distinguishable from the surrounding noise level.
(2) Every vehicle shall be equipped with two (2) rear-vision mirrors, one (1) at each side, firmly attached to the outside of the motor vehicle, and so located as to reflect to the driver a view of the highway to the rear, along both sides of the vehicle.
(r) A mobile food vendor may only sell food and non-alcoholic beverage items. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a mobile food vendor may offer alcoholic beverages for sale if the mobile food vendor is licensed to sell alcoholic beverages in accordance with the applicable provisions of the City of College Park Code of Ordinances. Alcoholic beverages offered for sale by a mobile food vendor may be consumed in public areas subject to the following conditions:
(1) If the alcoholic beverage is consumed in accordance with the provisions of section 3-3 of the City of College Park Code of Ordinances; or
(2) If the alcoholic beverage is consumed in such public areas as may be designated by the city as permissible for public consumption of alcohol.
(Ord. No. 2021-17, § 2, 12-6-21)
1148:
(a) Proof of pest control service.
(1) All applicants for an occupational tax license, or renewals of such shall provide required information and pay all applicable fees at the time the application is submitted;
(2) Prior to the issuance, or renewal of an occupational tax license, a copy of a twelve-month contract with a certified pest control service, registered with the State of Georgia, shall be provided;
(3) Prior to the issuance of an occupational tax license to new or existing establishments, the applicant shall provide evidence of satisfactory compliance with the provisions of this chapter and all other provisions of laws that apply to the location, construction and maintenance of food service establishments and the safety of persons therein.

(2) Food service establishments with drive-thru windows will post the current inspection report, and also have the inspection report posted so that a minimum of the top one-third of a copy of the current inspection report is visible through each window allowing customers to easily read the score, date of inspection and establishment information.

If requirements of this paragraph are not possible because of physical restrictions, a location will be determined as approved by the health authority.

(c) Property. The permit shall be returned within seven days to the local health authority when the food service establishment ceases to operate, has a change in ownership, is moved to another location or when the permit is revoked.
(d) Responsibilities of the permit holder. The permit holder shall:
(1) Post the permit as in a location in the food service establishment that is conspicuous to consumers;
(2) Comply with the provisions of this chapter including the conditions of a granted variance as specified under DPH Rule 511-6-1-.10(5)(a), and approved plans as specified under subsection (4)(b) of said rule;

(Ord. No. 2019-06, § 2, 4-15-19)
1151:
(a) Insurers license fees. There is hereby levied for the year 1985 and for each year thereafter an annual license fee upon each insurer (whether life or otherwise) doing business within the City of College Park in the amount of seventy-five dollars ($75.00). For each separate business location in excess of one (1) not covered by subsection (b), which is operating on behalf of such insurers within the City of College Park there is hereby levied a license fee in the amount of seventy-five dollars ($75.00). (b) License fee for insurers certain risks at additional business locations. For each separate business location, not otherwise subject to a license fee hereunder, operated and maintained by a business organization which is engaged in the business of lending money or transacting sales involving term financing and in connection with such loans or sales, offers, solicits or takes application for insurance through a licensed agent of an insurer for life insurance said insurer shall pay an additional license fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) per location for the year 1985 and for each year thereafter.

There is hereby levied for the year 1985 and for each year thereafter an annual license fee upon independent agencies and brokers for separate business location from which an insurance business is conducted and which is not subject to the company license fee imposed by subsection (a) hereof in the amount of seventy-five dollars ($75.00) for each such location within the City of College Park.

Gross direct premiums as used in this subsection shall mean gross direct premiums as used in Official Code of Georgia Annotated Section 33-8-8.2(a)
(f) Due date for license fees. License fees imposed in subsections (a), (b) and (c) of this section shall be due and payable on the 1st day of January, 1985 and on January 1 of each subsequent year.

(2) The premium taxes levied by section 14-121(d) and (e) hereof are due and payable upon January 1st of each year. Any company not reporting and paying the premium tax on or before forty-five (45) days from the 1st day of January for that particular taxable year shall be delinquent.

Such report shall be made over affidavit of an officer of such company. It is hereby declared to be a violation of this section for any person, firm, corporation or their agents to knowingly file false or incomplete information on any such report. Said report shall be filed at the time of paying the license fee and premium tax.
(4) The person responsible for each such insurance business location subject to license fee under section 14-121(c) hereof shall file with the city clerk a report, on forms prescribed by him, showing the address of the business location; the class or classes of insurance written; the names of the persons writing insurance at such location; the names of the companies represented; and such other reasonable information as may be required. Such report shall be made over affidavit of the person in charge of such business location. It is hereby declared to be a violation of this section for any person, firm, corporation or their agents to knowingly give false or incomplete information on any such report. Said report shall be filed at the time of paying the license fee.
(5) All reports required to be filed under this section shall be confidential and the information contained therein shall be solely for the use of the officers of the city responsible for administering this section.

In the event any portion of this section shall be declared or adjudged invalid or unconstitutional, it is the intention of the city council of the City of College Park that such adjudication shall in no manner affect the other sections, sentences, clauses or phrases of this section which shall remain in full force and effect, as if the invalid or unconstitutional section, sentence, clause or phrase were not originally a part of the section.
(k) Repealer. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this section are hereby repealed.
(Ord. No. 84-14, 8-6-84)

This article is intended to ensure compliance with applicable provisions of state law, promote transparency in the expenditure of public funds, and ensure that tourism-promotion funding is expended for the direct benefit of the City of College Park. Nothing contained herein shall be construed to create an entitlement to city funding or to limit the discretion of the city council in determining whether, when, or in what amount funding shall be awarded.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1157:
For purposes of this article, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:
City funds means any funds appropriated, distributed, granted, or otherwise provided by the city to a destination marketing organization.
Destination marketing organization or DMO means a private sector nonprofit organization or other private entity exempt from federal income taxation under section 501(c)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code whose primary responsibilities include promoting tourism, attracting visitors, encouraging conventions, meetings and events, and providing visitor assistance and support, as such definition may be amended under Georgia law.
Tourism promotion means activities intended to market, advertise, promote, attract, encourage, or increase visitation to the city.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1158:
(a) The city may designate one (1) or more destination marketing organizations through approval of a funding agreement, professional services agreement, grant agreement, or other written instrument authorized by the city council.
(b) Designation as a DMO shall be nonexclusive. Nothing contained herein shall be construed to require the city to designate, fund, or contract with only one (1) DMO.
(c) The city may designate, fund, and contract with one (1) or more destination marketing organizations, tourism promotion entities, nonprofit organizations, or other qualified entities authorized by law as determined by the city council to be in the best interests of the city.
(d) No designation shall confer any exclusive right to receive city funding, represent the city, or provide tourism promotion services on behalf of the city.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1160:
(a) No city funds shall be disbursed to a DMO absent a written agreement approved by the city council.
(b) The city council may allocate available tourism-promotion funding among one (1) or more destination marketing organizations in such amounts and upon such terms as deemed appropriate.
(c) Funding awarded under any agreement shall remain subject to annual appropriation by the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1161:
(a) City funds distributed pursuant to this article shall be used solely for lawful tourism-promotion purposes authorized under applicable Georgia law and approved by the city.
(b) Permissible uses may include destination marketing, tourism promotion, convention recruitment, visitor services, special-event promotion, tourism-product development, hospitality marketing, economic development activities directly related to tourism, and other lawful activities approved by the city.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1162:
(a) All city funds distributed pursuant to this article shall be expended solely for programs, services, activities, initiatives, events, marketing campaigns, tourism promotion efforts, tourism-product development activities, convention recruitment efforts, visitor services, or other lawful purposes that directly promote, support, market, develop, or otherwise benefit the city.
(b) City funds shall not be expended primarily for the promotion, marketing, operation, development, support, or benefit of another municipality, county, destination, attraction, event, facility, or tourism initiative unless specifically approved by the mayor and council and demonstrated to provide a direct and substantial benefit to the city.
(c) A DMO shall maintain accounting records sufficient to identify all expenditures made using city funds and to demonstrate the direct benefit of such expenditures to the city.
(d) City funds shall not be pooled, redistributed, allocated, or otherwise used in a manner that prevents the city from identifying how its funds were expended and how such expenditures benefited the city. The DMO shall maintain separate accounting records identifying all revenues received from the city and all expenditures made using such revenues.
(e) Any expenditure that cannot be adequately documented as providing a direct benefit to the city may be deemed an unauthorized expenditure.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1164:
Not less than ninety (90) days before the beginning of each fiscal year, each DMO receiving city funds shall submit a proposed annual budget and work program for review and approval by the mayor and council. The submission shall identify anticipated expenditures, proposed marketing activities, tourism initiatives, performance goals, measurable outcomes, and any other information requested by the city.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1166:
The city may establish annual performance measures including hotel room nights generated, event recruitment efforts, visitor engagement metrics, tourism-related economic impact indicators, website traffic, digital marketing performance, convention leads, and other tourism-promotion outcomes. Performance results may be considered in determining future funding allocations.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1167:
(a) Each DMO shall maintain complete books and records relating to all city funds.
(b) Such records shall be maintained for not less than seven (7) years.
(c) The city shall have the right to inspect, copy, and audit records relating to the receipt or expenditure of city funds.
(d) The DMO shall provide an annual independent financial audit prepared by a certified public accountant.
(e) The DMO shall fully cooperate with any audit, review, or investigation conducted by the city.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1168:
(a) Except as otherwise approved by the city council or provided in an approved expenditure plan, all city funds distributed to a DMO pursuant to this article shall be expended during the fiscal year in which such funds are received.
(b) The DMO may maintain a reasonable operating reserve; provided, however, that such reserve shall not exceed fifteen (15) percent of the city funds received by the DMO during the preceding fiscal year unless expressly authorized by the city council.
(c) Any city funds remaining unexpended at the conclusion of a fiscal year in excess of the reasonable operating reserve shall be expended pursuant to a written expenditure plan approved by the city council or shall be subject to return to the city upon demand.
(d) No DMO shall accumulate city funds for the purpose of creating unrestricted reserves, investment accounts, endowment funds, or other long-term fund balances not specifically authorized by the city council.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1169:
(a) Upon the expiration, termination, non-renewal, replacement, or other change in designation of a DMO receiving city funds, the former DMO shall return all unexpended city funds then in its possession, custody, or control to the city within five (5) business days of written demand by the city. Such funds shall be held in trust for the benefit of the city pending remittance.
(b) The former DMO shall simultaneously provide the city with a final accounting identifying all city funds received, expended, obligated, encumbered, reserved, or otherwise maintained by the DMO.
(c) The former DMO may retain only those city funds necessary to satisfy documented contractual obligations expressly authorized under a written agreement with the city and identified in the final accounting required herein.
(d) Any city finds retained pursuant to subsection (c) shall be remitted to the city immediately upon satisfaction, expiration, termination, or release of such contractual obligations.
(e) Following receipt of such funds, the city shall expend, administer, transfer, or otherwise utilize such funds in accordance with applicable law.
(f) Failure to comply with this section shall constitute a violation of this article and shall entitle the city to pursue all remedies available at law or equity, including recovery of funds, injunctive relief, and specific performance.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1170:
As a condition of receiving city funds pursuant to this article, each destination marketing organization shall provide one (1) non-voting ex officio seat on its governing board to a representative designated by the city council, who may be either a member of the city council or the city manager. The ex officio member shall be entitled to receive notice of all meetings of the governing board, copies of agendas and meeting materials provided to board members and may attend and participate in discussions of the governing board. The ex officio member shall not possess voting rights unless otherwise authorized by the organization's governing documents.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1171:
The city may require reimbursement of any city funds determined to have been expended in violation of this article, the applicable funding agreement, or applicable law. Such reimbursement obligation shall be cumulative of all other remedies available at law or equity.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1172:
If a DMO violates this article, violates a funding agreement with the city, fails to submit required reports, fails to maintain eligibility requirements, misuses city funds, or fails to demonstrate that city funds were expended for the direct benefit of the city, the city council may withhold future disbursements of city funds, require corrective action within a specified period of time, require reimbursement of improperly expended funds, terminate the applicable funding agreement, or determine that the entity is ineligible to receive future tourism-promotion funding from the city until compliance has been demonstrated. Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the authority of the city to contract with, fund, or otherwise utilize one (1) or more other qualified destination marketing organizations or tourism-promotion entities as authorized by applicable law and determined by the city council to be in the best interests of the city. Further, nothing in this section shall be construed to relieve, impair, or otherwise affect the city's obligation to expend hotel-motel tax revenues in accordance with applicable provisions of state law.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1173:
Each DMO receiving city funds shall annually present to the city council a report summarizing expenditures, activities, performance metrics, accomplishments, and objectives for the upcoming fiscal year.
(Ord. No. 2026-17, § 1(Exh. A), 6-1-26)
1176:

"Gross receipts" shall mean gross receipts as defined in O.C.G.A. § 48-6-90. 1178:
